title: Review: Lipids: triglycerides; Phospholipids, steroids and other lipids; Control of heart rate and ECGs; Food tests and chromatography
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: BM06#t2 term and clue written for the game; BM09a#t1 term and clue written for the game; BM09a#t2 term and clue written for the game; EX08#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: BM05#N.14, BM06#N.14, BM09a#N.13, EX08#N.7, BM05#N.3, BM06#N.9c, BM09a#N.14, EX08#N.10, BM09a#N.4a, EX08#N.14a. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Hydrophilic
items.clue: Describes the charged phosphate head, which interacts with water

items.label: Iodine test
items.clue: A change from orange-brown to blue-black shows that starch is present

items.label: Benedict's reagent
items.clue: Blue Cu²⁺ solution; forms a brick-red precipitate when heated with lactose

items.label: Atrioventricular node
items.clue: Only route through the non-conducting layer; delays the wave by about 0.1 s

questions.stem: To make a spread, manufacturers react a liquid vegetable oil with hydrogen, using a catalyst. Some C=C double bonds in its fatty acid chains become C–C single bonds. How does the oil change?

options.text: It becomes more liquid, as double bonds stiffen chains and hold molecules together.
It becomes more unsaturated, as it now carries more hydrogen atoms.
It becomes more solid, as straighter chains pack more closely together.
It becomes more solid, as the extra bonds need more heat to break when it melts.

questions.explanation: Fewer kinks, closer packing, stronger attractions between molecules: a higher melting point. A liquid oil becomes a soft solid, like butter in the hook.

questions.stem: Lipoproteins carry cholesterol and triglycerides in blood plasma, which is mostly water. Each lipoprotein has an oily core of cholesterol and triglyceride, surrounded by a single layer of phospholipids (with some proteins). How are the phospholipids in this layer most likely arranged?

options.text: Tails facing outwards into the plasma; heads facing inwards into the oily core.
Heads facing outwards into the plasma; tails pointing inwards into the oily core.
Tails joined to one another by covalent bonds, forming a rigid shell around the core.
Mixed evenly through the oily core, as phospholipids are entirely hydrophobic like cholesterol.

questions.stem: 1.0 cm³ of DCPIP is decolourised by 0.50 cm³ of a 1.0 mg cm⁻³ vitamin C solution. The same volume of DCPIP is decolourised by 2.5 cm³ of a fruit drink. What is the vitamin C concentration of the drink?

options.text: 5.0 mg cm⁻³
0.20 mg cm⁻³
1.25 mg cm⁻³
0.50 mg cm⁻³

questions.explanation: The DCPIP needs 0.50 cm³ × 1.0 mg cm⁻³ = 0.50 mg of vitamin C. The drink supplied that in 2.5 cm³: 0.50 ÷ 2.5 = 0.20 mg cm⁻³.

questions.stem: On an ECG recorded at 25 mm s⁻¹, the distance between two R peaks is 30 mm. What is the heart rate in beats per minute?
questions.explanation: R–R time = 30 ÷ 25 = 1.2 s. Rate = 60 ÷ 1.2 = 50 beats min⁻¹.

questions.stem: One glycerol molecule and three fatty acid molecules react by condensation to form one triglyceride. How much water is produced?

options.text: One water molecule is released
Three water molecules are released
Four water molecules are released
No water is released; water is used up

questions.explanation: Each –OH of glycerol reacts with the carboxyl group of one fatty acid in a separate condensation, forming an ester bond and releasing one water: three in total.

questions.stem: Cholesterol and other steroids do not contain fatty acids, yet they are classified as lipids along with fats and phospholipids. Which property shared by these molecules is the basis for grouping them together?

options.text: They are polymers, so each is built by joining many similar monomers.
They are rich in energy, so cells use them mainly as stores of fuel.
They are mostly non-polar, so they do not dissolve readily in water.
They are harmful, so cells are healthier with as few of them as possible.

questions.explanation: Lipids are grouped by a property, not a shared monomer: mostly C and H joined by non-polar bonds, so they are hydrophobic. A phospholipid has a polar head, but its two long tails are non-polar.

questions.stem: A sample of milk is tested. Heated with Benedict's reagent: an orange-red precipitate. With biuret reagent: lilac. With iodine in potassium iodide: stays orange-brown. Which conclusion is supported?

options.text: It contains glucose and no other sugar.
It contains starch, protein and a reducing sugar.
It contains a reducing sugar and protein, but no detectable lipid.
It contains a reducing sugar and protein, but no detectable starch.

questions.explanation: Precipitate: reducing sugar. Lilac: peptide bonds, so protein. No blue-black: no starch detected.

questions.stem: A person stands up quickly and their blood pressure falls for a few seconds. Which sequence describes the feedback response that restores blood pressure?

options.text: Baroreceptors in the arteries send fewer impulses to the medulla, which sends sympathetic impulses that raise heart rate and stroke volume.
Baroreceptors detect the fall and the medulla sends impulses along the vagus nerve to reduce heart rate, because a lower rate lets the pressure recover.
The medulla sends the impulses that cause each heartbeat more frequently, because the heart cannot beat at all unless the medulla drives it.
Baroreceptors in the heart wall detect the fall in pressure and the heart raises its own rate without any involvement of the medulla.

questions.stem: A solution gives a negative result with iodine. With Benedict's reagent, heated, it stays blue. A fresh sample is boiled with dilute hydrochloric acid, neutralised, and tested with Benedict's again: a brick-red precipitate forms. What does the solution contain?

options.text: A reducing sugar, because the final Benedict's test was positive.
Starch, which the acid broke down into glucose.
A non-reducing sugar, such as sucrose, and no reducing sugar.
A reducing sugar made by the acid joining smaller sugars by condensation.

questions.explanation: Negative first, positive after acid hydrolysis: the acid split a non-reducing sugar into reducing monosaccharides.

questions.stem: In a heart transplant, the nerves linking the donor heart to the medulla are cut, and they do not regrow for many months. Which statement about the transplanted heart is correct?

options.text: It cannot beat until the nerves regrow, because each beat needs an impulse from the brain.
It beats steadily, because its SAN starts each beat, but the medulla can no longer adjust its rate quickly.
Its rate still rises at once when blood pressure falls, because the baroreceptors are in the heart wall itself.
Its atria and ventricles now contract together, because nerves from the brain normally time the ventricles.
